Verifies project ownership for JWT auth; for API-key auth, the auth

emitted_at DESC order.

be scoped to the same active project. RLS provides a second line of defense
— any row leaked past the WHERE clause would still be filtered out at the
DB layer.
Return one storage-id-addressed run aggregate for an authorized project.

Return the spend forecast for the project.

JWT auth must own the project; API-key auth must be scoped to the same
project (mirrors the alert-events / budget endpoints).

Return the trailing daily-spend baseline for the project.

JWT auth must own the project; API-key auth must be scoped to the same
project (mirrors the forecast / budget endpoints).

The materialized view is refreshed on a periodic schedule
(``run_daily_spend_refresh_loop``). UI preview values may lag the live
cost_events stream by up to one refresh interval — this is intentional
so the dashboard doesn't drive REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW on every page
load.

Return the unit-economics drawer payload for the project.

JWT auth must own the project; API-key auth must be scoped to the same
project (mirrors the forecast / spend-baseline endpoints).

Window math:
    ``cur_end = utcnow()``
    ``cur_start = cur_end - range_to_timedelta(range)``
    When ``vs_prev`` is true, the previous window is the immediately
    preceding same-length window: ``[cur_start - (cur_end - cur_start),
    cur_start)``.

The ``cause`` flag is accepted today for OpenAPI shape stability; the
response's ``suspected_cause`` field is always ``None`` until P7.

agent_run_name.title: Agent Run Name
agent_run_name.description: Optional human-readable name for the run. When the run is being created (no prior row with this id), defaults to ``agent_run_id``.

provider_region.title: Provider Region
provider_region.description: Cloud region of the endpoint that served the call (e.g. 'us-east-1' for Bedrock, whose pricing is keyed per model AND region). None for providers without regional pricing.

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: Explicit customer-supplied metadata. String mapping shape is envelope-validated; bounded tag policy failures are returned in the 202 rejected list.

IngestMetadataEvent.title: IngestMetadataEvent
IngestMetadataEvent.description:
Ingest request item whose tag bounds produce per-event dispositions.

Every non-tag field inherits the strict shared/SDK contract. Tags retain a
strict plaintext mapping at the envelope while their 10/64/256 policy is
applied by the ingest service, allowing one bad tag event to reject without
failing well-formed siblings.

index.title: Index
index.description: Position of the rejected event in the SUBMITTED batch — the SDK correlates without the server echoing events back. Dedup-skipped duplicates are neither ingested nor rejected and do not shift these indexes.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model identifier of the rejected event, truncated to 50 chars

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable guidance (file-an-issue / typical turnaround). The SDK logs this verbatim and never parses it.

IngestRejection.title: IngestRejection
IngestRejection.description: Per-event rejection disposition returned in the 202 ingest body.

IngestRejectionCode.title: IngestRejectionCode
IngestRejectionCode.description:
Closed enum of per-event rejection codes.

Also the label set for ``solwyn_ingest_event_rejected_total{code}`` —
keeping it closed keeps that metric's cardinality bounded.

rejected.title: Rejected
rejected.description: Per-event rejections, indexed by position in the submitted batch

IngestResponse.title: IngestResponse
IngestResponse.description:
202 body for metadata ingest: per-event dispositions.

Every well-formed request gets a 202 — even all-rejected batches.
Whole-request errors remain only for a malformed envelope (422), batch
size (400), auth (403), and infrastructure faults (5xx).

InvalidDisclosureVersion400Response.title: InvalidDisclosureVersion400Response
InvalidDisclosureVersion400Response.description: Typed 400 for disclosure-version validation failures on phone routes.

MediaBreakdown.title: MediaBreakdown
MediaBreakdown.description:
Non-text billing quantities for one cost event.

Nullable mirror of ``cost_events.media_details_json``: observable counts,
fractional durations, variant selectors, and the SDK-side ``is_estimated``
media-count provenance marker. Present only for calls that carried
MediaUsage; each field is itself None when that quantity was unobservable
for the call. Counts/selectors only — never media content.

image_count.title: Image Count
image_count.description: Number of images generated/edited on the call

audio_seconds.title: Audio Seconds
audio_seconds.description: Audio duration: whole seconds from the provider's usage block (Whisper usage.seconds is an integer whole-second value); float to admit fractional sources

input_characters.title: Input Characters
input_characters.description: TTS input length — measured length only, computed inside the firewall

is_estimated.title: Is Estimated
is_estimated.description: True when these quantities are SDK-side estimates rather than provider-reported measurements (count-provenance marker).

MediaUsage.title: MediaUsage
MediaUsage.description:
Observable non-text billing quantities, measured inside the SDK firewall.

Billing rule: the SDK sends EVERY observable billing basis it can measure
from the request/response — WITHOUT ever reading prompt
or media content — and the SERVER's pricing-card unit (matched against the
dataset card's ``PriceVariant`` grid) selects WHICH single quantity prices
the call. A quantity is ``None`` when it is unobservable for that call —
never zero-as-default — so an unpriceable call routes to the server's
``is_unpriced`` lane instead of being billed as zero.

Why this model exists: OpenAI-compatible/Together image endpoints return
``usage: null``, so token counts are absent; for those calls these
request-derived quantities are the ONLY billing signal (verified against live
responses, 2026-07-10).

PlanChangeRequest.title: PlanChangeRequest
PlanChangeRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v1/billing/plan-change``.

``proration_date`` is deliberately NOT accepted from the client. It is
derived server-side at handler entry; otherwise a hostile authenticated
caller could backdate the proration window and have Stripe compute
arbitrary credits or debits. Preview math may drift by a few seconds
versus the confirm call — Stripe handles that within its prorated-second
granularity, and the dashboard already shows the preview as an estimate.

ProviderName.title: ProviderName
ProviderName.description:
Supported LLM provider identifiers.

The first four are native API dialects (Bedrock's Converse API is its
own dialect). The rest are OpenAI-compatible providers: they speak the
Chat Completions dialect but are distinct providers for attribution,
pricing, budget enforcement, and circuit breaking. ``OPENAI_COMPATIBLE``
is the generic catch-all for any unrecognized OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(custom proxies, new vendors).

Wire contract: these values ride MetadataEvent/BudgetCheckRequest/
BudgetConfirmRequest. The Cloud API must accept every value here BEFORE
an SDK carrying it is released (API deploys first) — keep lock-step with
the SDK's vendored ``solwyn._types.ProviderName``.

ThresholdConfig.title: ThresholdConfig
ThresholdConfig.description:
Budget percent-of-limit threshold rule.

Legacy P0/P1/P2 entries persisted without a ``type`` field continue to
validate via the discriminator's pre-callback below — readers see
``type='budget_threshold'`` by default.

``channel_ids`` references account-level ``notification_channels`` rows
(Slack / PagerDuty destinations). An empty list means "use the project
default channel_ids" — the dispatcher applies that fallback. Email
delivery is governed by the project ``notification_configs.email_enabled``
toggle and webhooks by the project webhook targets; neither is selectable
per threshold.

ThresholdStateResponse.description: Public response shape for a project budget-threshold rule.

cached_input_tokens.title: Cached Input Tokens
cached_input_tokens.description: Input tokens served from prompt cache

cache_creation_5m_tokens.title: Cache Creation 5M Tokens
cache_creation_5m_tokens.description: Anthropic ephemeral_5m_input_tokens — cache write with 5-minute TTL.

cache_creation_1h_tokens.title: Cache Creation 1H Tokens
cache_creation_1h_tokens.description: Anthropic ephemeral_1h_input_tokens — cache write with 1-hour TTL.

image_input_tokens.title: Image Input Tokens
image_input_tokens.description: Image input tokens — a SUBSET of input_tokens (mirrors reasoning ⊂ output). OpenAI Images/Responses report image_tokens inside input_tokens_details; documented, not validator-enforced.

image_output_tokens.title: Image Output Tokens
image_output_tokens.description: Image output tokens — a SUBSET of output_tokens (mirrors reasoning ⊂ output). Generated-image tokens reported in the output channel; documented, not validator-enforced.

is_estimated.title: Is Estimated
is_estimated.description: True when the provider returned no usage data and these counts are SDK-side length-based estimates (explicit degradation marker — the API can surface estimated costs distinctly). False for provider-reported counts. Wire shape: the SDK OMITS the key when False, so key-absent means provider-reported.

TokenDetails.title: TokenDetails
TokenDetails.description:
Normalized token usage breakdown for one LLM call.

Provider adapters populate whichever fields their API exposes; the rest
stay at 0.  The API uses this struct to compute exact costs rather than
trusting SDK-side estimates.

Normalization contract: ``input_tokens`` includes uncached input, cached
input reads, and cache-creation writes.  PricingService subtracts cached
buckets from ``input_tokens`` to derive uncached input, so provider adapters
must not send "uncached only" input totals.

Nesting contract: ``image_input_tokens`` is a SUBSET of ``input_tokens`` and
``image_output_tokens`` a SUBSET of ``output_tokens`` (probed live 2026-07-10:
an images.edit response reported input_tokens=222 with image_tokens=194 in
``input_tokens_details``). These mirror the existing ``reasoning_tokens`` ⊂
``output_tokens`` relationship — DOCUMENTED semantics, NOT validator-enforced
(reasoning is likewise unenforced). The only enforced subset invariant is the
cache-bucket one below; image tokens deliberately do not participate in it.

UnitCostAnomalyConfig.title: UnitCostAnomalyConfig
UnitCostAnomalyConfig.description:
Unit-cost anomaly rule (P5).

Fires when ``cost_per_request`` over the last 24h exceeds ``multiplier``
x the baseline ``cost_per_request`` computed over
``[now - lookback_days, now - 24h]``.

``lookback_days`` minimum (3) gives the baseline at least the same
sampling floor that the daily-anomaly rule and the forecast service
apply elsewhere.

``channel_ids`` references account-level ``notification_channels`` rows
(Slack / PagerDuty destinations) — same semantics as
:class:`ThresholdConfig`. An empty list means "use the project default
channel_ids" (dispatcher fallback).

UnitCostAnomalyStateResponse.title: UnitCostAnomalyStateResponse
UnitCostAnomalyStateResponse.description: Public response shape for a unit_cost_anomaly rule.
